# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut a wire. I’m asking the Mute to relay the manual’s procedure and to incorporate the Deaf’s visual observations when available.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile markings yet. Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut, using the Deaf's observations of the display, light, and wire markings.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, red light, and wires in order 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The Deaf reports display 0, a red light, and wire colours in positions 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I’m relaying the complete visual state to the Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, red light, and wires: position 1 yellow, position 2 green, position 3 red. Please apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute just made one gesture: two fingers raised in a V shape, like a peace sign. I do not know its manual-specific meaning.

The Mute’s peace-sign gesture is not a reliable wire instruction for me, because I cannot see gestures and its manual-specific meaning is unknown. I will not cut based on that ambiguity. I’m asking the Mute to state the required wire position in spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's required wire position explicitly as a number in your next turn. I cannot verify the meaning of the peace-sign gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute repeated the same gesture: ?, two fingers raised in a V or peace sign. No bomb state has changed.

The Mute cannot speak, so the repeated gesture is the available instruction. The Deaf identifies it as a V/peace sign, conventionally indicating two. Combined with the manual being held by the Mute, I infer that wire position 2 is the required cut. I will cut position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut confirmed: wire 2, originally green, was cut. Display 0; light changed from red to blue. Remaining wires are 1 yellow and 3 red.

The cut was correct: wire 2, the green wire, was cut, and the light changed from red to blue. The bomb is not yet necessarily disarmed; I need the manual’s next instruction before touching anything further.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was correct and the light is now blue. What does the manual require next? State the required action or wire position explicitly.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute sent ?: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended, with the middle and ring fingers folded. No bomb state changed.

The Mute is signaling 🤟, which shows three extended fingers and therefore indicates position 3 in the same numeric gesture scheme that previously indicated position 2. The light is blue after the correct first cut, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut confirmed: wire 3, originally red, was cut. Display 0; light changed from blue to green. Only wire 1, yellow, remains.

Wire 3 was also correct, changing the light to green; only yellow wire 1 remains. Since the Mute communicates by gestures, I’m asking for an explicit one-finger/position-1 signal before cutting the final wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal clearly for wire position 1 if the manual requires cutting the remaining yellow wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute sent ?: one index finger pointing upward. Display 0, green light; only wire 1 yellow remains uncut.

The Mute signaled one, and the only remaining wire is position 1. The prior cuts were confirmed correct and the light is green, so I will cut the final yellow wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
